It is currently at the dealership for the third time, where it has been for more than a week. The car has spent, in total, almost 30 days in the service department while we have had a loaner. The dealership has replaced the battery at least once. As far as we know the service department cannot diagnose the Question and has only been able to repeat it once. We have never been given a reason for the repeated loss of power, even when the battery is fully charged. The dealership has not contacted us in almost a week and we have not been given an update on the status of the car. We are fed up, the car is unfixable and we would like to explore legal options under Oregon's Lemon Law, as it applies, even though we live in Fairhaven.

For example, one allegation was made , as written in the initial “request acknowledgment “ where the claim states that I referred the client to my uncle for an assessment. When I showed that this was not possible, since my uncle died two years prior, the investigator said in a recorded phone call that she did not need my response or to discuss it because it “was just a misunderstanding.” When I received the legal documents outlining the allegations and sanctions, the allegation had changed to I made her feel uncomfortable and confused by going on and on about my uncle. It is clear that once I could prove the allegation was untrue, the client’s story changed. The Board should have noted from there that she is an unreliable reporter. However, there were several other allegations that the Board took as true. The type that I cannot provide proof I did not do or say. But again, the way the investigator presented the allegations, I could not answer because I could not recall such generalities. When given the legal documents with details, I can say that I did not, and would not have done such things. I want to request a hearing and need advice as to whether I should have an attorney represent me, and if there is any point to pursuing a hearing based on the case information.

It was my account so we (2 of us) was on the phone with the gentleman & heard what he said. He stated he will put a note our files and we could just go to the nearest store and return the phone & get another phone. When we got to the store, the lady read the gentleman's notes and he stated that he told us we couldn't get the restocking fee waived, & that we understood. That was a lie.....I am now angry & they won't give us back the money for any transaction. I am very upset that TMOBILE is doing this to their customers and it needs to stop. I just want my $ back.

I tried to fight them in the beginning but woman there was obstinate and called me a liar? Asked for a hearing that I was unable to attend. I was found guilty when I wasn't guilty at all, employer didn't have another job for me but unemployment says they offered me another job? They did not. I really don't want to have to pay additional $3,000 in interest and penalties and lose all of my income tax returns. Next they will try to garnish wages and I was just able to begin working again. Had surgery in June and couldn't return to work for 6 months. Thanks.
